This is an application for recalling of the order dated  February 28, 2024 passed in C.O. No.2971 of 2023.
Affidavit of service indicates that the petitioner  attempted to serve his wife but she refused service.

Thus,
 the matter is taken up in her absence, as refusal is good  service.

The order dated September 15, 2022 passed by the  learned Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 1st Court at  Paschim Medinipur, in Judicial Misc. Case No.03 of 2022  was under challenge in the civil revisional application.

sentences.text: By the order impugned, the learned court dismissed  the matrimonial suit as withdrawn at the instance of the  applicant Sri Tarapada Mandal, but directed permanent  2 alimony of Rs.10,500/- per month.
The husband, the petitioner herein, challenged the said order on various grounds.
According to him, without a decree for divorce permanent alimony could not be granted.
He was represented by his learned Advocates before the revisional court.
Before the revisional court, the learned Advocate for the wife submitted that Rs.7,000/- was being paid by the petitioner until the suit was withdrawn.
That the wife and the child would be left in a vagrant condition and they did not have any means of sustenance.
The child is 15 years old.
As soon as the application had been filed for enhancement of the maintenance pendente lite, the petitioner withdrew the suit.

Upon hearing the parties, this Court was of the view that the withdrawal of the suit after 10 years from its filing and after having dragged the wife and the child the Court should not have been allowed without some cost to the wife.

However, the revisional held that the order of the learned trial Judge directing permanent alimony, deserved Sri Tarapada Mandaal vs Smt. Tarunita Mandal on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190251700/
2 to be set aside.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court could not direct the permanent alimony of Rs.10,500/- per month to be paid by the petitioner.

3  The petitioner was successful in the said revisional application, but the Court took a view that the wife and the child had to go through lot of physical and mental harassment and a social stigma was also attached to the entire issue, as a woman from a middle class family, was dragged to court by her husband, for such a long period of time.
It was also recorded by the Court that she had no source of income.
A litigant has dragged another party to court and compelled the party to contest the proceedings.
She invested time, money, her emotion and her reputation was at stake.
The withdrawal of the suit should not be a matter of course.

Under such circumstances, cost of Rs.2,00,000/-
was directed to be paid to the wife and the child in four equal monthly instalments.

This order is sought to be recalled on the following grounds:
 (a) The wife is unwilling to reside with the petitioner.
(b) The wife has initiated several litigations against the  petitioner.

(c) A false case under Section 498A of the Indian Penal  Code was filed against the petitioner, from which Sri Tarapada Mandaal vs Smt. Tarunita Mandal on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190251700/
3  the petitioner has since been acquitted.

sentences.text: 4  (d) Other proceedings under the Domestic Violence  Act and under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal  Procedure are pending against the petitioner.
(e) Most importantly, the wife has proceeded for  execution of the order grating permanent alimony.
It appears that cost was given by this Court upon holding that the order allowing permanent alimony deserved to be set aside by the Court, but a direction to that effect was inadvertently missed out.

Although, the body of the order clearly indicates that this Court was of the view that the order of permanent alimony deserved to be set aside, but cost of Rs.2,00,000/- to be paid to the wife for the harassment caused to her.

Under such circumstances, the order is modified to the extent that, towards the end of the order, after paragraph 10, the following paragraph be inserted:-
 1.

The order dated September 15, 2022 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 1st Court at Paschim Medinipur in Judicial Misc. Case No.03 of 2022, to the extent of directing permanent alimony of Rs.10,500/- per month to be paid to the wife, is set aside.
